premises: Composition changes in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys modulate stacking fault energy (SFE).
SFE governs the relative prevalence of deformation twinning versus dislocation slip.
Deformation mechanism (twinning vs. slip) is the primary factor controlling strain hardening, strength, and ductility.
Lower SFE promotes deformation twinning, leading to enhanced strain hardening and strength.
Quaternary/ternary alloys can achieve an optimal SFE for a desired strength-ductility balance.
